definitions.explanation: Porcelain produced in and around the town of {有田|ありた} in Saga Prefecture. Japan's first true porcelain, with a 400-year tradition, known for fine white clay and intricate cobalt-blue or polychrome decoration.

examples.japanese: {有田焼|ありたやき}の{皿|さら}を{買|か}った。
examples.english: I bought an Arita ware plate.

examples.japanese: {有田焼|ありたやき}は{白|しろ}と{青|あお}の{絵付|えつ}けが{有名|ゆうめい}だ。
examples.english: Arita ware is famous for its white-and-blue decoration.

examples.japanese: {祖母|そぼ}から{譲|ゆず}り{受|う}けた{有田焼|ありたやき}の{茶碗|ちゃわん}を{大切|たいせつ}に{使|つか}っている。
examples.english: I treasure the Arita ware tea bowl I inherited from my grandmother.

notes:
Named after the town of {有田|ありた} in Saga Prefecture, Kyushu. Produced since the early 1600s, when porcelain clay was discovered in the area.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Until the late 19th century, Arita ware exported through the nearby port of {伊万里|いまり} was called {伊万里|いまり}{焼|やき} in foreign markets. The two names overlap but in modern Japanese {有田焼|ありたやき} usually refers to the porcelain made in the Arita region, while {伊万里|いまり}{焼|やき} now more often refers to older pieces or pieces in classical styles.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {有田焼|ありたやき}の{茶碗|ちゃわん}: Arita ware tea bowl
- {有田焼|ありたやき}の{皿|さら}: Arita ware plate
- {有田焼|ありたやき}{窯元|かまもと}: Arita ware kiln/workshop
